subdomain: 3.8 Evaluate progressive discovery vs. monolithic context strategy

en.question: An application uses the documented standard server-side tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119 pattern with Claude Messages API 2023-06-01. Its catalog contains deferred application-executed tools, and no custom external catalog service is involved. Which requirements remain true after progressive discovery is enabled? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Return a client tool_result for the search's server_tool_use ID before running any discovered business tool.
options.note: Built-in tool search runs server-side and returns its own search-result block. The application must not invent a client result for that server-side search ID.

options.text: Supply every deferred tool's complete definition in the tools array on every request in this standard pattern.
options.note: defer_loading controls what initially enters model context, not whether definitions are sent to the API. The API needs the catalog to search and expand tool_reference blocks.

options.text: Execute a discovered client tool when its tool_use arrives, then continue with its matching tool_result and preserved assistant content.
options.note: Discovery supplies the definition but does not execute the application's operation. Ordinary client-tool execution, result correlation, and conversation continuation still apply.

options.text: Omit discovered definitions from later requests because their expanded references are a durable server-side catalog registration.
options.note: Inline references do not replace the standard request's required definitions. The API expands references using the tools supplied in each request, not a durable implicit catalog registration.
